summary.text: A male infant with Dowling–Meara epidermolysis bullosa simplex was born at 37 weeks 6 days by scheduled Cesarean section for breech presentation, birth weight 2191 g, Apgar scores 8 and 9. He had extensive epidermal detachment at birth, was admitted to the NICU, had relative hypoproteinemia and received albumin and globulin preparations and red cell concentrates. Respiratory status was on room air until 45 days of age, after which oxygenation declined with tracheomalacia and supplemental oxygen was delivered.

Positional changes were initially prohibited and parental visits restricted for COVID-19, with restrictions easing from postnatal day 65. Habilitation and rehabilitation began with minimal contact, using positioning, minimal ROM exercises, wound dressings and caregiver instruction; nasal CPAP was started at 148 days and prone positioning on day 156, and ventilation support was upgraded to SiPAP in the NICU stay before transfer to the Growing Care Unit on postnatal day 210.

Motor milestones were delayed relative to the standard months in Table 1. By discharge on postnatal day 311 he had stable head and neck control, reaching, rolling with prompting and sitting with minimal support and stable oxygenation, while crawling and standing remained challenging and mild trunk hypertonicity and ROM limitation persisted. No adverse events occurred during rehabilitation, and parents received home instructions at discharge.
